predecessors.name: Almoravid dynasty
predecessors.text: the High Atlas around Tinmel, inside the Almoravid realm: 'Ibn Tumart abandoned his cave in 1122' and 'established his base at Tinmel' around 1124

successors.name: Marinid Sultanate
successors.text: Morocco: the Marinids took Meknes (1244 or 1245), Fez (1248), Sijilmassa (1255) and Marrakesh (1269)

successors.name: Hafsid dynasty
successors.text: Ifriqiya (Tunisia, Tripolitania and eastern Algeria): the governor Abu Zakariya declared independence in 1229

successors.name: Zayyanid dynasty
successors.text: the Kingdom of Tlemcen, independent around 1236

successors.name: Taifa of Murcia
successors.text: Murcia, Almeria and the rest of Almohad Spain and Portugal, 'Ibn Hud and the other local Andalusian strongmen', from October 1228

successors.name: Taifa of Valencia
successors.text: Valencia, taken by Zayyan ibn Mardanish after the Almohads left in 1228

ledger.x: 1121: Ibn Tumart founds the Almohad movement in the High Atlas.
1132: the Almohads conquer Aghmat.
1139: the Almohads expand into the Rif.
1144: Tlemcen falls to the Almohads.
March 1145: Oran falls and Tashfin dies.
1146: Fez falls after a nine-month siege.
1147: Marrakesh falls and the Almoravid dynasty ends.
1147: the remaining Almoravid Morocco passes to the Almohads.
1147: the capital moves from Tinmel to Marrakesh (infobox 'Marrakesh (1147-1269)').
1147: Abd al-Mu'min's army takes Algeciras and Tarifa, the first Almohad foothold in Iberia.
1148: Seville falls to the Almohads.
1149: Cordoba falls to the Almohads.
1152: the Badajoz taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
1152: the Niebla taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
1152: the Saltes and Huelva taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
1152: the Carmona taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
1152: the Cordoba (second taifa) taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
1152: the Denia taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
1152: the Tejada taifa's land is Almohad in Cliopatria.
August 1152: the Almohads take Bejaia and end the Hammadid kingdom.
1155: the last Almoravids in Granada are defeated.
1157: Almeria passes from Castile to the Almohads.
1159: the Almohads take Tunis.
1158-1159: the Norman towns of coastal Ifriqiya are abandoned to the Almohads except Mahdia.
1160: Tripoli recognises Almohad authority.
January 1160: Mahdia surrenders and the Norman Kingdom of Africa ends.
1172: the Almohads take Murcia.
1172: the Almohads take Valencia with Murcia.
November 1184: the Banu Ghaniya invade and occupy the Almohad east.
1185: the Almohads retake the Balearic Islands.
By 1187: the Banu Ghaniya recover the Balearics.
1188: Cliopatria's shape drops 67 Iberian cells held in 1177 (Caceres 38, Badajoz 19, Ciudad Real 4, Teruel 3, Castellon 3).
1188: Yaqub al-Mansur reconquers Ifriqiya and the occupation ends.
1189: Portugal takes Silves.
July 1191: al-Mansur recaptures Silves.
1195: after the Battle of Alarcos (18 July 1195) the Almohads take back Trujillo and Montanchez.
1202: Cliopatria's shape adds 24 more cells (Badajoz 19, Ciudad Real 4, Toledo 1).
1203: the Almohads take the Balearic Islands for good.
January 1206: Mahdia surrenders to the Almohads.
16 July 1212: Las Navas de Tolosa.
1216: more of the Iberian interior leaves the Almohads.
1217: Alcacer do Sal falls to Portugal.

1227: Cliopatria's shape drops 77 cells held in 1220: 50 in Badajoz province, which the correction puts back (the Almohad page's 'Merida and Badajoz in 1230 (to Leon)' is a Christian conquest after al-Ma'mun left Seville in October 1228, so Badajoz cannot have gone to Leon in 1227; it leaves with the rest of Iberia in…
1228: Murcia leaves the Almohads.
1228: Almohad rule in Valencia ends.
1228: Almeria passes from the Almohads to Ibn Hud.
October 1228: Almohad rule in Iberia ends.
1229: Ifriqiya breaks away.
1230: Constantine and Bejaia go to the Hafsids.
1230: Mallorca falls to Aragon.
1235: Algiers falls to the Hafsids.
1236: Tlemcen becomes independent under the Zayyanids.
1244: the Marinids take Meknes.
By 1248: the Marinids take Taza, Rabat and Salé.
1248: the Marinids take Fez.
1255: the Marinids take Sijilmassa.
1269: the rest of Almohad Morocco passes to the Marinids with Marrakesh.
1269: the Marinids take Marrakesh and the Almohad Caliphate ends.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the Almoravid realm
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: the Almoravids crushed the Almohads at al-Buhayra in April or May 1130, Ibn Tumart died in August 1130, then Aghmat fell in 1132, Tlemcen in 1144, Fez in 1146 and Marrakesh in 1147.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of Al-Andalus
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: 'Between 1146 and 1173, the Almohads gradually wrested control'; Algeciras 1147, Seville 1148, Cordoba 1149, Granada 1155, Murcia 1172.

wars.name: Almohad conquest of the Hammadids and Norman Africa
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Bejaia August 1152, Setif April 1153 (a rout of the Arab tribes), Tunis March 1159, Mahdia January 1160, Tripoli 1160.

wars.name: Banu Ghaniya campaigns in Ifriqiya and the Balearics
wars.outcome: Almohad victory: Ifriqiya reconquered 1187-1188; Balearics retaken 1185, lost again by 1187, taken for good in 1203; raids continue to 1237/1238; Mahdia surrenders in January 1206 after the October 1205 battle at Jabal Tajra (Muhammad al-Nasir page).

wars.name: Almohad campaigns against Portugal and Castile (Silves, Alarcos)
wars.outcome: Almohad victories: Silves, taken by Portugal in 1189, recaptured by al-Mansur in July 1191 after a campaign of about 15 months; Alarcos, 18 July 1195, after which 'the Almohads reconquered Trujillo, Montanchez, and Talavera'; the raids of 1195-1197 'did not…

wars.name: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
wars.outcome: Christian victory on 16 July 1212: al-Nasir withdrew to Marrakesh; Baeza and Ubeda fell shortly after; 'By 1252 the Almohad empire was almost finished.'

wars.name: Marinid conquest of Morocco
wars.outcome: Marinid victory: Meknes 1244 or 1245, Fez 1248, Sijilmassa 1255, Marrakesh 1269.

wars.name: Christian conquests in Almohad Spain
wars.outcome: Christian gains: Alcacer do Sal 1217 and Mallorca 1230 (the Balearics 1228-1232 on the Las Navas page).

certainty.note: An Atlas guerilla zone and then a patchwork of conquered towns; the pages give cities, never frontiers.
Approximate frontiers throughout: the Saharan edge, the Castilian and Portuguese frontier (soft though a truce was bought from Ferdinand III for 300,000 maravedis), and the Ifriqiya-Libya limit.

sources.title: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
Abu Yusuf Yaqub ibn Abd al-Haqq
